Commentary.Commentary: There isn't anything wrong with the surface but there is some extra bounce which is always expected at the WACA. Australia will have to bat sensibly against the new ball and then take it forward. Dale Steyn and Co. would like to make life difficult for the Australians. Stay tuned for a great battle between bat and ball. David Warner and Shaun Marsh will be out soon as around 24 overs are still left in the day's play.

The South African top half was completely blown away. Faf du Plessis gutted out for a while and the partnership between Bavuma and de Kock was the only substantial stand they managed. Temba was very impressive in his stay while de Kock just carried on with his brilliant form. The manner in which he batted was simply outstanding but he got a few lives as well.

Terrific bowling effort by the Aussies! They have bundled out South Africa to a below par total courtesy some great all-round bowling. Mitchell Starc was absolutely on fire and finished with a 4-fer while his new ball partner, Josh Hazlewood claimed a 3-wicket haul. The rest of the bowlers also impressed and it was a team effort totally by Australia. Their fielding was also top notch, however, there were a few chances which went down.

OUT! Bowled 'em! You miss buddy and I hit! Starc steams in from around the wicket and spears in a fuller length ball on middle, it's fast and furious, Steyn makes space but fails to keep it out and finds his stumps shattered. SOUTH AFRICA ARE ALL OUT FOR 242!
Mid off comes in and leg gully moves to covers. Khawaja from short leg helps himself to mid on.
Digs another shorter one, around middle, Steyn sways away from the line of fire.
Starc switches to over the wicket and angled across a shortish ball outside off, Steyn swishes and misses.
Rabada has looked comfortable while playing the short balls. Starc serves one around off, Kagiso stands tall on his back foot and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

FOUR! Mitchell Marsh nearly pulled out another stunner! Shortish and outside off, Rabada goes back to push inside the line and edges it behind. Marsh flies to his right at gully and it goes just wide of his outstretched right hand for a boundary. Vital runs these!

FOUR! Well timed! Drops it on a length and angling away from the batsman, Rabada stays back and pushes it with an angled bat. Nice timing and more importantly it's well placed right through the gap between point and gully for a boundary.
Good variation of length, goes short and on middle, Rabada tries to take it on with the pull shot but the bounce gets big on him and beats the top edge.
Keeps it full and just around off, Kagiso defends it compactly with his bat and pad put together.
Angles across a length ball outside off, Rabada pushes at it and misses.

FOUR! Shot! Full in length and around off, Steyn gets forward and plays a punchy drives through the line. It comes from the middle of the bat and races through the vacant mid off region for a boundary.
Fine shot! Short and around leg, Rabada plays a controlled pull shot down to fine leg for a single.
Fast and furious delivery, on back of a length around leg, Rabada gets in a tangle as he fends at it. Probably a leading edge but it doesn't carry to gully.
Good length ball angling away from the batsman from around the wicket, Rabada drops his wrists and allows it through to the keeper.
Action replay of the previous delivery, another bouncer, Rabada sits underneath it.
Starc takes Rabada by surprise by banging in one short around leg, he's ducked.
Dale Steyn is the last batsman.

OUT! Quinton de Kock misses out on a deserving century! Hazlewood digs in a shortish ball on middle, de Kock swivels with the pull shot but it comes from the higher part of the bat and balloons in the air. Shaun Marsh moves back a bit from short mid-wicket and takes a simple catch. End of a wonderful knock by de Kock, he batted without much issues and dominated the Aussie bowlers.
Four byes! Hazlewood bangs in a short ball and it goes well over the batsman. Nevill jumps but fails to collect it cleanly. It goes off his gloves to the fence.
Fullish and on middle, pushed down the ground to mid on.
Appeal for an lbw! Angles in a length ball on middle and leg, going down, de Kock fails to work it around and is hit on the pads. They appeal but it's missing leg.
Shortish and outside off, de Kock camps back to cut it through the line and Mitchell Marsh at gully makes a diving stop.
Full and angling into the batsman, Rabada flicks it off his pads to the leg side, finds mid-wicket.
Kagiso Rabada is the new batsman.

OUT! Maharaj holes out! A loopy full ball around off, Maharaj advances down the track to loft it over long on but fails to get the timing right. Warner takes the skier calmly and ends Maharaj's short stay. Wasn't to the pitch of the ball there, Keshav. The fielding effort on the last ball by Khawaja was also the key there. It's a team sport.
Loopy and full around off, driven through cover-point for a single. Khawaja was quick to the ball and kept them down to only one run.
Short and on off, cut straight to point.
Floated full ball on middle, de Kock gets forward and defends it back.
Flighted and full on off, it's driven through covers and the fielder in the deep slides to make a sliding stop. They manage to come back for the second.
Bowls it short and around off, de Kock goes deep inside the crease and cuts it straight to point.
Full in length and around off, Maharaj stays back and pushes it to covers.
On a good length around off, angling in a bit, Maharaj covers the line and allows it through to the keeper.
PLAY AND A MISS! A little bit of width on offer outside off, Maharaj camps back to slap it through point but fails to make any connection.
Short and wide outside off, de Kock stands back and slaps it through point for a single.
Josh switches to around the wicket for de Kock and angles in a full ball on off, it's driven to covers.
Full and angling into the batsman, Maharaj pushes it wide of mid off and crosses for a single. Wants the second run but Warner is quickly to the ball.
Fires in a quicker one on off, de Kock forces it out to point. Good comeback ball by Lyon!
FOUR! Nicely played! Loopy ball around off, Quinton kneels and nails his slog sweep over mid-wicket. Makes fine connection and sends it screaming to the fence.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! de Kock continues his merry way! Advances down the track to take it on the full and whips it across the line. The mid-wicket fielder dives to make a half stop but it still races through and beats the chase put in by Hazlewood from mid on.
Full flighted ball on off, it's driven off the front foot but straight to covers.
Flighted ball on off, de Kock defends it off his front foot.
Nathan Lyon is back on.
Bangs it short around off, Maharaj ducks to evade it.
Switches to over the wicket and bowls a fuller length ball on middle and off, Maharaj gets forward and defends it close to his front pad. A stare from Starc!

SIX! Ho! Ho! Ho! Starc serves a touch short ball around off, Maharaj clears his front leg and dismisses it over the bowler's head for a biggie. That came out of nowhere. Waiting for Starc's response now who will be angry at the moment.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Short and on middle, pulled down to fine leg where the fielder picked it late but did manage to stop the ball. A single taken.
Wide called for height! Starc digs in a short ball and it goes well over the head of the batsman.

FOUR! Starc has DROPPED the return catch! de Kock gets another life, third to be precise. A couple of run out chances missed and now a catch goes down. Full in length and outside off, de Kock stays back and hits it firmly across the line. It goes aerially and quickly past the bowler who tries to take the catch but it bursts through his hands and speeds away to the fence.
A touch short on off, it's punched off the back foot through covers for a couple of runs.
Tucks a length ball through square leg for a single.

NOT OUT! Hazlewood slants in a length ball on off, angling in, de Kock tries to heave it across the line but misses and is hit on the back leg. They appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Steven Smith goes for the referral. The third umpire first confirms that there is no inside edge and then says that the impact is with the umpire's call. The next statement seals the deal which is - It's going over the stumps. Australia have lost both their reviews now.
Shout for an lbw. Not given and the Aussie skipper takes the referral.
Fuller in length and angling into the batsman, it's driven back to the bowler.
A touch short and outside off, de Kock camps back to cut but misses.

FOUR! That has just raced through! Hazlewood also bowls short to de Kock, his pace is never going to trouble the batsman and the southpaw pulls it disdainfully to the deep mid-wicket fence. The replays show that it hit the bat twice. The Hot Spot confirms that too. It reminds me of my childhood when double bat used to be out in gully cricket.
Short and around off, pulled in front of square leg for a single.
Starc continues to bowl short to de Kock, around leg and the batsman ducks.
A controlled push of the bat to a full ball and it races through the gap at covers for three runs.

RUN OUT CHANCE OF DE KOCK MISSED! Full in length and angling into the batsman, Maharaj pushes it from the crease to covers and sets off for a single. de Kock also responds and is mid-way down the track when Keshav stutters after seeing Lyon get to the ball. He sends his partner back but de Kock has no chance of returning safely unless the fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end. Luckily for South Africa it happens and Quinton survives.
Digs in a short ball on middle, de Kock swivels on the back foot and pulls it to deep backward square leg for a single. Brave batting!

SIX! High and handsome! Starc continues to target the rib cage of de Kock, it's short and the batsman looks to pull but gets a top edge. The ball sails over fine leg for a biggie. Fighting fire with fire, Quinton.
Play and a miss! A touch short in length and outside off, holding its line, Maharaj throws his bat at it and misses.
Drops it on a length and around off, Keshav goes back in defense and it comes off the bottom half of the bat. It nearly rolls onto the stumps.
Stifled appeal for an lbw! Length ball on middle, angling in, Maharaj tries to defend but misses and is hit on the thigh pad. They appeal but it's too high and also going down.

FOUR! Off the mark in Test cricket! Good length ball landing around off, Maharaj has a gentle push inside the line from the back foot and it runs off the outside half of the bat through gully. The fielder chases (Khawaja) but the ball wins the race.
Walks across the stumps to a length ball and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Back of a length ball on off, de Kock drags it off the inner half of the bat to mid on.
Josh Hazlewood to bowl from the other end.
On a length and outside off, angling in, Maharaj stays back and goes down to duck. Starc smiles.
Angles in a short ball on off, Maharaj leans back and allows it through to the keeper.
A very full ball on off, Maharaj digs it out to the off side.
Back for the last session. The players are back on the field. 38 overs are still left in the day's play. Keshav Maharaj has joined de Kock. Mitchell Starc to continue...
...DAY 1, THIRD SESSION...

As far as Australia are concerned, finishing the job will the main concern. As he saying goes - Well begun is half done. But you need to end what you started. They will be looking to wrap up the tail quickly and then bat out the day. 37.3 overs left, so it is going to be a long session. Join us back at 1300 IST (0730 GMT).

Starc started the session with the wicket of du Plessis and also ended it, claiming Philander. In between, de Kock and Bavuma had a wonderful 71-run stand for the 6th wicket before Shaun Marsh's blinder broke it. The South African keeper has looked in excellent touch and will look to bat with the tail and score as much as possible.

Boredom is not a word for watchers of the Aus-SA Test. Or even the players. It seemed like the Proteas have the game under control, threading decent partnerships but then wickets in the last half an hour have brought the game back to life. Australia conceded 97 RUNS IN 26.3 OVERS in this session but those three wickets have just put them in front.

OUT! DRAGS IT ON! Starc has struck moments before Tea. A poor shot from Philander, one has to say. A length ball outside off, not all that short, Philander looks to pull but there is no feet movement and he gets a thick inside edge onto his stumps. Starc is pumped up, he has got his third wicket. And to think he has just come off a nasty injury. TEA ON DAY 1!
A short ball, pulled down to long leg for a single.
A bouncer around off, de Kock ducks.

RUN OUT CHANCE! MISSED! Down the leg side, Philander tucks it towards square leg. He takes a couple of steps for the run and de Kock charges but then Philander sends him back. David Warner charges to the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Replays show that de Kock would have been short even with a dive.
Full and down the leg side, flicked towards backward square leg.
Reaches out and pushes this past the bowler, sets off for a single but quickly shouts, "WAIT ON!" seeing mid on cover it up.
Lunges forward to this one and blocks.
Full and outside off, defended forward.
Landed outside off, defended in front of short leg.
5th Test Fifty for de Kock! He continues his superb form.
FOUR! That is a cracking shot. A length ball outside off, de Kock pulls this through mid-wicket for a boundary!
The batsman just manages to keep the yorker out. Good ball bowled by the bowler. The batsmen have run through for a single.
A short ball down the leg side, pulled over a leaping Nathan Lyon at leg gully towards fine leg for a single.
The batsman does well to leave that bouncer.

NOT OUT. Nothing on the Hot Spot. A length ball down the leg side, de Kock looks to tickle it fine but misses. The ball deviates off something and Smith goes for the review after Nevill agrees. Replays detect thigh pad.
Is that a wicket? Australia claim they have de Kock. The umpire does not agree and the hosts have reviewed for what they think is a catch down the leg side.
Some chin music for the batsman, he lets that bouncer through to the wicket-keeper.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full on middle, worked past short leg towards mid-wicket.
Down the leg side, worked straight to backward square leg.
FOUR! That is an amazing shot. Landed outside off, Philander goes back and punches it through the covers for a boundary!
Landed outside off, Philander dead-bats it.
Full and outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
A short ball but way down the leg side, Quinton sways away from the line.
A testing bouncer, around leg, de Kock ducks.
Full on middle and leg, pushed with a straight bat-face towards mid on.
On middle and leg, worked through square leg for a single. That was poor running. Peter Siddle had to run a long way to his left from fine leg and the batsmen could have taken the second.
Around off, angling away, left alone.
A length ball down the leg side, Philander lets it through.
The batsman has edged that one through slips. One run added to the total.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

That is a terrific stop. That was the way he got his fifth wicket in his first Test. Full and around off, VP punches this down the ground but Lyon flies to his right and stops it cleanly, colliding into de Kock. Loses control over the ball due to the collision but recovers well. Real superman.
Full and around off, clipped towards short mid-wicket.
Down the leg side, Vernon lets it through.
Full and outside off, Philander leans and works it towards short mid-wicket.

CRICKET UPDATE - We don't want you to turn your attention from this compelling Test but it is our duty to keep you updated about cricket all across the globe. International, at least. Moving over to Sharjah, West Indies have completed a thrilling Test win over Pakistan to avoid a whitewash and end the series 1-2. Kraigg Brathwaite was the star, with a century in the first innings and a half century in the second, unbeaten throughout the match! Back to the WACA now.
A short ball around middle and leg, Quinton looks to tuck it to the leg side but is beaten and is hit on the chest.
A bouncer now, de Kock ducks.
Another short ball, QdK defends it with a hop.
A short ball, around the rib cage, Quinton hops and defends it in front of square leg.
This is fuller but on middle and leg, de Kock shuffles across and tickles it towards fine leg for a couple. The stand moves to 10 from just 16 balls.
Backward point moves to third man now.
A length ball outside off, climbs alarmingly, de Kock lets it through.
MITCHELL STARC comes back on for a quick burst. Australia would want de Kock before Tea.
Landed outside off, defended towards short leg.
Now he holds the length back and de Kock goes back and works it towards fine leg for a run.
Better length, closer to the batsman, bit of drift as well, taking some pace off too. de Kock drives it towards short extra cover.
Fired in on off, whipped wide of mid on for a single.
On middle and off, Vernon keeps it down in front of short leg.
Tossed up outside off, Philander comes forward and defends.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Outside off, watchfully kept out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, left alone.

FOUR! de Kock continues to be in Fantasy land. On a pitch where his team mates have struggled to be confident. Full and outside off, de Kock comes forward and threads this through the covers for a boundary.

Poor captaincy from Smith. Unless he expected Philander to go big on his very first ball. Or perhaps he forgot that the new batsman is on strike. There is a long on in place and Philander calmly pushes this towards that fielder for a single. Ideally, that fielder should have been at mid on, saving the single.
VERNON PHILANDER walks in at number 8, probably a touch earlier than he would have expected.

OUT! That is a stunner! Wow. Goodness me. Both the Marsh brothers have taken blinders in the field today. Earlier, it was Mitchell in the first over and now, it is the elder brother Shaun. Landed around off, perhaps a touch short, Bavuma stays back to turn it around the corner but gets an inside edge. The ball hits him on his thigh pad and goes towards the leg side. Shaun Marsh at short leg, dives to his right, his wrong side and takes it inches above the ground! Nevill appeals, so does Lyon, the umpire asks them to wait but Bavuma is not bothered. He walks off! End of an enterprising stand and Australia are into the lower order.
Full and outside off again, Temba is down the track once more and drives it back to the bowler who mimes a shy at the striker's end.
Third Test Fifty for Bavuma! He has played really well, not letting the situation get to him.

FOUR! Elegant! What a way to get to his half century. Tossed up outside off, Bavuma comes down the track and drives it beautifully through the covers for a boundary! The stand moves to 71 from just 92 balls.
Full on middle, de Kock stays inside the line and pushes it through the covers. Usman Khawaja ambles after it and what should have been a couple, turns into three.
NATHAN LYON comes back into the attack as well. Smith realizes that apart from run-rate, he has to control the over-rate as well.
On a good length outside off, angling in, Temba lets it go. That was not far from the off stump.
Full and outside off, a touch wide, left alone.
Outside off, tapped to the off side for a quick run.

Close call. Full and outside off, Temba pushes it towards mid off and scurries through for a single. David Warner is the man over there, quickly gets to his left, has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Bavuma had dived in though.
Interesting. Walks across his stumps and pushes it towards short mid-wicket.
On a good length outside off, Bavuma looks to punch it on the up and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
PETER SIDDLE is back on. Australia need some control.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Good length ball outside off, it's punched off the back foot to gully. Straight to Starc.
Full in length and outside off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Pitches it full outside off, de Kock gets forward and drives it with good timing through covers. Lyon moves across to his left in the deep and stops the ball. A couple of runs taken.
Lands it full and outside off, de Kock drives it through the gap at covers for a brace.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller in length outside off, a careful cover drive by Bavuma, through the gap and they take a couple of runs.
Bouncer around off, Bavuma picks the length early and just moves away from the line.
FOUR! Bavuma, you little beauty boy! An overpitched delivery outside off, Temba leans into the drive and caresses it with all the elegance through extra cover for a boundary.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
de Kock has played it to the point region. One run added to the total.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. No run.

FOUR! The little batsman is growing in confidence in de Kock's company. Marsh digs in a short ball on off, not quite the pace to trouble the batsman, Temba eases himself on the back foot and pulls it powerfully over mid-wicket for a boundary. The sip of water has done wonders to his strike rate it seems. A couple of boundaries to his name in this over. 50-run stand comes up in quick time!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Cracking shot! Full in length and outside off, Bavuma plays it with a little front foot movement but backs it up with good timing. Connects well and sends it whistling through point for a boundary.

EDGED BUT SAFE! Good length ball angling into the batsman and gets it to straighten a touch, Bavuma stands back to play inside the line. He does so with soft hands and as a result the outside edge doesn't carry to the slip cordon.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
A little bit of away movement outside off, Bavuma feels for it and gets beaten.

Drinks break. 46/1 in the first hour after lunch. Australia started well but the current partnership is trying hard to revive South Africa. Quinton de Kock has certainly provided an impetus to the scoring rate and has raced to 31 in no time. The Aussies would like to see his back sooner than later while the visitors will hope that he stays there for as long as possible. Not to ignore Bavuma's contribution, he has batted nicely however he looked a bit tentative after lunch.
An overpitched ball on off, de Kock whips it through square leg for a couple of runs.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Slants across a length ball on off, angling away, de Kock gets forward and across and leaves it untouched.
Angles across a full ball wide outside off, it's left alone by de Kock.
Good running between the wickets. Length ball on off, Bavuma stands back and taps it down to covers for a quick run.
Fuller in length and around off, angling away, de Kock gets forward, opens the face of the bat and pushes it through cover-point for a single.
Width on offer outside off, Bavuma slaps it with all his power but finds the backward point fielder.

Nearly drags it on! It would have been a huge wicket for Australia. Poor shot by de Kock, he chases a wide delivery outside off and gets a big inside edge past the stumps. It runs down to fine leg and they take a single. This was the closest Marsh got to picking a wicket.
Serves it full and outside off, it's driven off the front foot to mid off.
Shortish and on off, de Kock strokes it firmly past the left side of the short cover fielder. Warner chases it from mid off and keeps them down to two.
Kevin Pietersen (on air) feels that with good wind blowing across the ground, it won't be too long before we see Nathan Lyon into the attack.
A touch short and on off, it's punched from the crease to mid off.
Angles across a good length ball on off, de Kock moves closer to the line of the delivery and pushes it to covers.
A little bit fuller on off, Bavuma is careful into the drive and keeps it out to covers.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
This one is a harmless delivery. Full and way wide outside off, left with ease by Bavuma.
Nicely done. Fetches a length ball from outside off and wristly turns it to mid-wicket for a single.
Angles across a full ball outside off, Quinton gets across the stumps and defends it on the leg side.
Bowls it full and around off, de Kock gets across the stumps and defends it with his bat and pad together.
Full and outside off, de Kock slapped it square of the wicket and picked up a single.
Tickles it wide of mid on and returns for the second run.

Serves it full and around off, slips in the process and goes down on ground, the batsman is not distracted though and drives it off his front foot to mid off. Hopefully, Mitchell Marsh has not done any damage to himself. He is very injury prone as we all know.
Play and a miss! de Kock needs to be very careful with his shot selection. He just cannot keep throwing his bat at everything. Width on offer outside off, Quinton flashes and misses.

Turns a length ball to the right side of the mid on fielder and crosses for a single. Siddle moves across swiftly to the stop the ball, there is a confusion over the second run and de Kock eventually is sent back.
Full in length and outside off, it's left alone by Bavuma.
Mitchell Marsh is back on as well.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.

FOUR! Boom! No stopping this one. Hazlewood clocks 140.7 kph and bowls it full and wide outside off, Quinton strides forward and drives it crisply through through covers for a boundary. This guy just carrying on with his good form.

EDGY FOUR! Identical to the last delivery, a bit too wide and de Kock goes after it with a full flow of his bat. He fails to middle it and the outside edge flies to the left side of third slip. Shaun Marsh tries to stop it on one bounce with a dive but misses and it sneaks past him to the fence.
Beaten! Fuller in length and around off, zipping off the surface, de Kock pushes inside the line and misses.
Bowls it on the middle stump line, a little bit of swing, Bavuma tickles it through mid-wicket and runs the first run hard. But while trying to turn for the second run he slips.
Starts with a length ball on off, Bavuma defends it from the crease.
Josh Hazlewood is back into the attack, replacing Siddle.
Gets hurried up there by the sharp pace and movement. Angling in a length ball around off, de Kock tries working it on the leg side but misses and is hit on the thigh pad.
Starc is playing on de Kock's patience here. Serves it full and keeps it outside off, there to be driven but Quinton shows a lot of patience in leaving it untouched.
False shot! de Kock goes chasing after a length ball wide outside off and misses. Lapse in concentration.
Digs in a bouncer around off, de Kock ducks underneath it.

Chance of a run out! Good length ball on off, Bavuma forces it through the line towards mid off and sets off for a single. Warner latches onto the ball and has a shy at the striker's end but it hits de Kock on his boots.
Temba Bavuma pulls out at the last moment and immediately apologizes to the bowler and the other Australian fielders. There is a fly which is causing some discomfort to the little batsman.
Played to the point region by the batsman. No run.

FOUR! Shot! Full in length and around off, de Kock gets across the stumps and punches it down the ground. The mid on fielder moves across to his right but decides not to put in the dive. It races through and Warner sprints behind it. But he fails to pull it back as the ball wins the race. Had that mid on fielder put in some effort and got even a hand to it, Warner would have stopped it.
Good length ball on off, de Kock defends it off his back foot to short cover.
Full and sliding down the leg side, Bavuma shuffles across the stumps and eases it through backward square leg for a single.
On a good length and around off, holding its line, Bavuma leaves it alone for the keeper.
Keeps it on a fuller length around off, Bavuma defends it tentatively to the leg side.
Angles in a full ball on middle and leg, Bavuma plays it from the pads to mid on.
Full in length and outside off, Bavuma pushes it to covers for a single.
A scorching bouncer, well-directed, Bavuma sways away from the line of fire at the last moment. Starc stands there and gives a stare. Just letting the batsman know who is the boss!
A lovely shot but straight to the fielder. Fuller in length and around off, Bavuma gets forward and pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fullish around off, Bavuma pushes it down towards mid on.

Starc runs in from around the wicket and bowls it from wide of the crease. A good yorker on off, 132.6 kph and Bavuma digs it out towards point. Lyon charges to the ball and Temba sends his partner back immediately.
Good length ball angling into the batsman from around the wicket, Quinton goes on the back foot and defends it to the leg side.
FOUR! Shot! This one is hit firmly off the front foot. Siddle keeps his length full but is probably too wide there. Width is on offer and de Kock obliges with a cracking cover drive.

FOUR! Pristine timing and this time de Kock gets the placement right! Gets on the front foot to a full ball, opens the face of the bat at the last moment and pushes it with great timing past the right side of the point fielder.
Poor delivery and Siddle gets away with it. On the pads and it's flicked to deep backward square for a single.
Full in length and outside off, shaping away just a shade, Bavuma watches the line closely before leaving it.
Bavuma has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Back of a length delivery sliding down the leg side, a harmless one, de Kock allows it through to the keeper.

Another very good shot for no run. This time it's due to the brilliance of Lyon at point. de Kock plays a crunchy square drive to a full ball, well timed and it's frustrating for the batsman that he doesn't get anything for it.
Drops it on a length and just outside off, de Kock sticks to his crease and defends it off the bottom half of the bat.
No run has come off this shot but it shows the kind of form de Kock is in! Fullish and outside off, Quinton gets forward and plays a free flowing drive. Finds the point fielder.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Nearly chops it on! Siddle bowls it on a full length and outside off, Bavuma with unsure footwork remains back and then decides to leave it. He is late though and it goes off the inner half of the bat, misses the stumps by a whisker and speeds away to the fine leg fence.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Angles across a full ball outside off, de Kock gets forward and tries to play through the line. But it catches the inside edge of the bat and rolls towards square leg for one.
Back of a length delivery on off, Quinton defends it off his back foot.
Angles in a good length ball on middle and leg, it's nudged to fine leg for a single.
QUINTON DE KOCK comes in at number 7, replacing du Plessis.

OUT! Starc strikes soon after lunch! Starc dishes out a back of a length delivery outside off, du Plessis rocks back and tries to force the issue through covers. But it seems the ball has moved a touch to take an outside edge. It flies to the right of first slip where Voges reacts quickly and grabs a two-handed catch. A good looking 49-run stand has been broken and South Africa have now lost half their side. du Plessis showed great level of patience till this ball and is disappointed with himself. Trudges back now.
Angles in a full length ball on middle, du Plessis defends it from the crease to mid-wicket.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Serves it on a length and wide outside off, it's left alone by du Plessis.

Age is just a number, the old guy proves it to the younger one. Fuller in length and angling into the batsman, Bavuma flicks it across the line to square leg where Khawaja dives to his left to make a partial stop. It still races through and Usman puts in a chase. He ambles behind it and Siddle also runs across to his left from fine leg. He reaches first, the old guy mind you, and puts in a dive to pull it back. Khawaja does the rest of the job and they take three runs.
Starts it with a length delivery outside off, Bavuma pushes it from the crease towards point where the fielder dives to his right and makes the stop.
Mitchell Starc is unleashed from the other end. Three slips for him along with a gully. He will bowl from around the wicket.
Steady line and length, in the corridor of uncertainty, good judgement by du Plessis before he leaves it.
Hurls it quite wide outside off this time, an easy leave for the South African skipper.
Angles in a full length ball on off, once again it's dealt with a straight dead bat by Faf.
Swinging in a bit, full and around off, du Plessis brings a straight bat down and defends it solidly.
Back of a length ball on off, Faf goes on the back foot and defends it down on the off side.
Full in length and angling into the batsman, on middle, du Plessis gets forward and across to flick it towards mid on.
We're back for the afternoon session. The men concerned are back in the middle. Peter Siddle to operate first up. A couple of slips in place along with a gully.
...DAY 1, SECOND SESSION...

We have seen it all in the first session. Wickets, dropped catches, mix-ups, run out chances and runs. As a watcher, can we ask for more? You bet we can be greedy. We still have two sessions in the day. What will happen after Lunch? Will Australia be able to break this stubborn stand quickly? Or will the Proteas continue their fightback? There is batting till Dale Steyn so the visiting side will hope for some good partnerships. Join us back at 1040 IST (0510 GMT) for the post-lunch session.

Starc removed Cook for a duck after squaring him up, but half of that credit should go to Mitchell Marsh who plucked a stunner. Amla then fell to Hazlewood, being unsure of his footwork, only to be followed by Elgar and Duminy. It was a terrific opening hour for Australia and the Proteas looked all at sea. But since then, du Plessis and Bavuma have battled hard and added 46, which has soothed the nerves. To be honest, the hosts were not that consistent after drinks.
It really looks like he writes the script, doesn't it? First over of a Test, ODI or a T20I. If it is Mitchell Starc, the batting side more often than not, loses a wicket. And it happened today again.

You might be anywhere in the world, you could belong to any country, but you can never miss out of action when Australia and South Africa battle it out against each other. It is fire versus fire and boy, did we see plenty of it in this opening session! With 4 wickets, it has gone in Australia's favour, especially having lost the toss.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended. LUNCH ON DAY 1!

Comes down the track and pushes it down the ground, past Lyon through mid on. Mitchell Starc dives to his left and stops it well. The batsmen take a single. Having just recovered from a knee injury, he might want to avoid such diving.
Stays right back in his crease and defends.
Comes down the track now and flicks it straight to short mid-wicket.
Comes forward a touch, then goes back after getting deceived in flight. The ball goes off the top half of the bat towards point.
Full and outside off, du Plessis comes forward and defends.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh pad.
FOUR! That is not a bad ball. Generates extra bounce after pitching on middle, Bavuma hops and nudges it to the fine leg fence. That could have so easily gone into Nevill's gloves.

OUCH. That would have hurt. A short ball around middle, Bavuma hops to tuck it away but misses and is hit on the rib cage. He wants a single but then slips as he is sent back. Could have been run out as Hazlewood kicks the ball towards the stumps. Misses it though. Bavuma is down in pain.
Full and outside off, pushed back to the bowler who leaps to stop.
Landed outside off, Bavuma shoulders arms. The ball suddenly generates good carry and bounce and almost goes off the toe end of the bat towards the keeper.
Full and outside off, Bavuma stays in his crease and blocks.

Short and outside off, Temba punches this in front of point. There is a single on offer and Faf wants it but Bavuma hesitates. There is a mix up and a run out opportunity as well. The fielder gets to the ball but then Bavuma runs like his life depended on it and makes it easily. Immediately raises his hand to his skipper and apologizes.
Full and outside off, driven straight to short extra cover.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off again, Bavuma stretches forward and pushes it towards covers.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid on for a single.
Full and outside off, left alone.
Outside off, punched wide of point towards covers for a single.
A short ball, pulled through to fine leg for a run.
A short ball now, outside off, Bavuma takes his hands away from the line and shoulders arms.
Comes forward and pushes it straight to cover.
Full and outside off, left alone.
Full and on middle, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, watchfully bowled.
FOUR! Wrong line, landed on middle, angling down the leg side, du Plessis just tickles it to the fine leg fence.
Eventually gets the single as he works this behind square leg.
Temba flicks it through the leg side but Marsh at short leg stops it with his left hand.
Full and outside off, Bavuma works it with the angle towards Shaun Marsh at short leg.
Shane Warne gets his wish. He wanted spin to make its presence felt and here comes NATHAN LYON.
FOUR! Crisp! What a shot. Full on middle, Faf drives it through mid on. The fielder dives to his left but such is the timing that the ball goes through. The stand moves to 32 and Faf moves to 30.
Full and just around off, watchfully defended.
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Wow. Excellent running again. Full and outside off, Bavuma drives it through the covers and takes the third run after the fielder is ready to throw. That is the perfect way to run. Keep on running till the ball rolls along the ground but then take that extra on the throw, especially if the man is in the deep. Of course, Ricky Ponting will disagree after what happened to him against Chris Mpofu in the 2011 World Cup against Zimbabwe where he was run out via a direct hit from deep mid-wicket, at the non-striker's end.
Steven Smith ringing in the changes. JOSH HAZLEWOOD comes back on.
Around off, angling in, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Played to the point region by the batsman.

Three leaves in a row, that is an art in itself, says Mark Nicholas on air. One should understand the needs of the WACA. Would have loved to hear more had he elaborated but.... my luck is not that good. Or he must have said and I might have missed it. Either ways, my bad.
Full again, very good channel, Faf allows it to go past as the ball shapes away.
Full and outside off, defended to the off side.

That is a beauty. Perhaps one of the rare ones in the last 40 minutes. After an excellent start, Australia have not quite been able to keep up to that level, especially since Drinks. On a good length outside off, du Plessis comes forward to defend but then the ball shapes away to square him up and beat the outside edge.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Landed outside off, watchfully pushed back towards mid off.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
WIDE. Wayward ball. Starc has not been that good in this spell at all. This is sprayed so wide outside off, even two Bavumas would not have reached it. The umpire stretches his arms.

Short and outside off, Faf gets on top of the bounce and punches it wide of mid off. David Warner gives it a chase and perhaps the ball got intimidated by his presence as he was haring after it. The cherry stops near the ropes and Warner slides to officially stop it. Three runs taken.

That is a nice way to defend, albeit would love to know how he did that. Full and around off, du Plessis comes forward to defend and then, his back leg goes in the air in his follow-through. Interesting.
A short ball down the leg side, du Plessis helps it through backward square leg for a couple. The stand moves to 21 from just 35 balls. Has kept the scoreboard ticking.
Short and outside off, punched wide of mid off for a run.

Mark Nicholas on air laments about the Australian over-rate being alarmingly low. 11.4 to the hour, he says. Very poor. May be, accounting those 4 wickets and the review, a slight consideration may be given but still...
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full on middle, driven straight to mid on.

That is an excellent single. Siddle goes fuller and just outside off, Temba just blocks it by coming forward towards cover. Sees the mid off fielder taking it a bit easy and immediately calls for the single and scampers through. 50 FOR SOUTH AFRICA.
On a good length outside off, Bavuma rides with the bounce and pushes it to point.

Good point from Ian Chappell on air. He observes that even though South Africa are 4 down for not many, the Aussies have to be careful. The reason? Because the next man to come in is Quinton de Kock who is in prolific form. If he comes in early, he might well decide to counter-attack and that might take the game away. So Chappell warns the Aussies against getting complacent after doing so well with the new ball.
The batsman worked this wide of mid-wicket for a single.
On middle and leg, worked wide of mid on for a single.
A bouncer, FdP bails out of the pull.
A short ball now, good bounce, Faf jumps and punches it to point.
Full and outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Classy! Full and outside off, du Plessis comes forward and drives it through the covers. The fielder gives it a chase from mid off but the ball wins the race. That is the beauty of batting in Perth. Because of the bounce, the ball comes on to the bat nicely and then this excellent outfield does the rest. All you have to do as a batsman is to survive those first 30-40 minutes and then bed in.
On a good length around middle, Faf keeps it down.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Short and outside off, Temba looks to repeat what Faf did on the previous ball but cannot find the gap. Hits it straight to cover.

Smart. Gets really deep in his crease, waits for the ball to come to him and taps it towards cover. The fielder throws the ball to Peter Nevill but it hits the stumps instead and deflects to square leg. Bavuma wants the second off the overthrow but the fielder comes in quickly and du Plessis sends Bavuma back.
Oohhh... that nearly sneaked through. Full and outside off, du Plessis comes forward to defend but the ball nips back in, takes the inside edge and hits him on the pads.
Full and outside off, defended back to the bowler.
FOUR! Clubbed! A short ball outside off, du Plessis stands back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. That just sat up and asked to be hit. Faf obliged. The stand moves to 10.
PETER SIDDLE comes on from the other end.
Full on middle, Bavuma works it through mid-wicket. He initially thinks there is just a single on offer but then spots the gap and charges back for the second.
Yorker outside off, jammed towards point. He has come in with an attitude to score, which is excellent in this scenario. Normally, teams tend to bog down in such situations.

Ian Healy on air feels that Mitchell Starc needs to be a bit more patient. One cannot be expecting to take wickets every ball. Fair point. But then, when you see your opposition 4 down under 40, you would be tempted to make it 5 down.
Full and outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Off the mark with ease. Full on middle, swinging in, Bavuma comes forward, covers the line and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Better, angles this away from the right-hander after pitching this on off, Bavuma trusts the bounce and movement and shoulders arms.
A loosener, full and down the leg side, Bavuma misses his flick.
MITCHELL STARC is back, after an excellent first spell. He had removed Cook in his opening over, who claimed that he feels at home at the WACA, as it reminds him about the Wanderers.
This is wider outside off, not played at yet. A better over from Mitchell Marsh.

Excellent point from Michael Clarke on air. He says that you can have lots of talks in the dressing room, on the ground, about the lines and lengths, etc... but execution is the key and Australian bowlers have been splendid with that today. Absolutely.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
One more leave outside off. Faf very conscious about his off stump.
Landed outside off, angling in, left alone.
Short in length outside off, punched on the bounce towards point.
Landed outside off, left alone.
On a length and around off, Temba defends it with an angled bat to point.
Fuller in length and on off, driven back to the bowler off the front foot.
Once again Bavuma has left a delivery outside off.
Good length ball outside off, Bavuma allows it through to the keeper.
Temba Bavuma, a batsman with short stature walks in next to join his skipper.
DRINKS BREAK.

OUT! Technology backs Australia and South Africa are reduced to 32/4! Beauty of a delivery by the old warhorse! On a full length and angling away from the batsman after landing around middle. Duminy gets forward to defend but it whizzes past the inside edge to the keeper. There is some sound as Nevill catches the ball and he screams in an appeal. The finger goes up and Duminy takes the DRS. The third umpire watches multiple replays and after getting the evidence from the Hot Spot he keeps the onfield decision as it is. A faint edge on the replays and Duminy walks back. First hour totally has belonged to the home side.
JP Duminy is given out caught behind. He has referred it upstairs...
Siddle drops it on a fuller length around off, Duminy tries to drive it through covers but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Length ball angling into the batsman, du Plessis stays back and forces it down to mid on.
A leg stump half-volley by Marsh, Faf plays a well-timed flick shot but finds the square leg fielder.
Back of a length delivery just around off, shooting off the surface with extra bounce, Faf covers the line and allows it through to the keeper.
Angles in a full ball on off, du Plessis strides forward and pushes it back to the bowler.
FOUR! Shot! This will calm down some nerves. Marsh dares to bowl short with a gentle pace, du Plessis rocks back with the pull shot and nails it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Starts well. Bowls it on a length and around off, good bounce, Faf stands back inside the crease and defends it down.
Mitchell Marsh replaces Hazlewood in the attack.
A touch short on this occasion but the line remains the same, around off, du Plessis plays it with gentle hands towards extra cover and scampers across for a single.
Identical to the last delivery, du Plessis allows the ball to come at him and then dead bats it.
Full and angling into the batsman, du Plessis defends it by getting a bit forward.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Lands it on a fuller length outside off, du Plessis walks across the stumps and shoulders arms. Appreciable inward movement as it passes the batsman.
Serves a full length ball outside off, du Plessis covers the line and leaves it alone.
Full and angling into the batsman, du Plessis flicks it off his pads and it goes through the gap at mid-wicket. Good running between the wickets to pick up three runs.
In the zone outside off, du Plessis chooses to leave the ball.
Nearly another wicket! Hazlewood alters his length and goes very full. Angles it in, du Plessis falls over to the off side as he attempts to flick but gets a big inside edge onto the pads.
du Plessis has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Bowls it on a fuller length outside off, shaping away a shade, du Plessis strides forward and leaves it alone. It moves quite a bit after leaving the batsman.
Angles in a length ball on middle and leg, good bounce, 135.3 kph, du Plessis tries defending from the crease but misses and is hit on the thigh pad.
Good length ball on off, Duminy gets across the stumps a bit and defends it down safely.
Defends it with gentle hands to the leg side, it rolls in the gap at mid-wicket and they pinch a single. The skipper is off the mark.

South Africa in tatters here. However, the batsmen dismissed have to blame themselves more than some excellent bowling. Have a look at JP Duminy. He has shown some decisive footwork. The rest have been caught somewhere in the crease.
Full in length and outside off, Faf defends it by getting half-forward.

DROPPED BY LYON! A good attempt by the off spinner but he could have done better. Siddle angles across a full ball outside off, Duminy leans into a loose drive and slices it in the air off the outside half of the bat. It bobbles up towards point where Lyon dives to his left and attempts to take a one-handed catch. However, he fails to grab it and the ball gets deflected behind. They take three runs.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and angling into the pads, Duminy plays it on the leg side but straight to the fielder.
Here comes the workhorse, PETER SIDDLE.
Skipper Faf du Plessis walks in next with his team in early trouble.

OUT! Elgar falls! It's going from bad to worse for South Africa. The top three batsmen are back in the hut with just 20 runs on the board. Hazlewood hurls across a length ball just outside off, angling away, Elgar goes back and has a tame push inside the line after getting squared up. He tries withdrawing his bat at the last moment but it seems he's too late. The keeper collects the ball, they appeal and the finger goes up. Elgar walks up to his partner, has a chat with him but Duminy advises not to waste the review. Anyway, it has to be Elgar's call as he will be knowing best whether he got an edge or not. Dean walks back and Snicko detects a spike there. Fair call in the end. Hazlewood gets his second wicket and Australia have taken an early advantage in this Test match. Best possible start.

Hazlewood serves it full and wide outside off, Duminy this time decides to play a booming cover drive but fails to middle it. The ball rolls in the gap though and by the time the mid off fielder gets to it, they take a single.
Good line, around off and angling away from the batsman, Duminy covers the line by taking his front leg forward and then leaves it alone.
Switches to over the wicket for Duminy and bowls a fuller length ball on off, it's driven off the front foot to mid off where the fielder makes a diving stop.
Brings a full ball back into the batsman, some extra bounce on this occasion, Elgar plays it with a loose bottom hand and helps it down to fine leg for a single.
Hazlewood operates from around the wicket. Bowls it on a length and outside off, Elgar has a watchful leave.
Full in length and angling into the batsman, Duminy brings a straight bat down in defense.
It's a tempter this time by Starc. He sprays it full and wide outside off, inviting the batsman to have a go, Duminy restrains himself from driving away from the body.
Bowling in terrific areas, this one is on the off stump line, skidding into the batsman off the surface, not offering much space to JP who defends it back from the crease.
Mitchell Starc runs in but pulls out at the last moment. Maybe he lost his run-up. Will have to reload.
This is a huge opportunity for JP Duminy. With four centuries in 56 Test inns, he hasn't quite cemented his spot yet. With not much experience in the middle order, he needs to step up today.
PLAY AND A MISS! Beautiful line and length outside off, shaping away with the seam, Duminy decides to drive it through the line but is beaten for pace and movement.
Turns it away, past short leg this time and a run is taken.

DROPPED! Starc angles in a full ball on middle and leg, Elgar leans across with the flick shot and it goes aerial to the left side of the short leg fielder. Khawaja gets a hand to it but it refuses to stick. A chance definitely has gone down but those catches just get stuck or they don't.
Full in length and outside off, Duminy lunges, opens the face of the bat and pushes it towards point.
Duminy has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fullish around off, Duminy gets on the front foot and pushes it back to the bowler off the inner half of the bat.
Hazlewood digs in a short ball on middle, Duminy decides to give respect and bows down to it.
Full and angling across the left-hander, it's a little too wide to make the batsman play.
Full in length and around middle and off, Duminy defends it from the crease to the off side. Very tentative footwork shown by JP.
Did you know? This is the 10th time that South Africa have lost a wicket against Australia without a run on the board! 8 times it happened back home just the second time here after the MCG in 1932!
Good length ball on off, angling in Elgar defends it off his back foot to end the over.
Digs in a fast bouncer to push the batsman deep inside the crease, Elgar stays back and ducks.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Another shot played off the inside edge by JP! Back of a length delivery on off, moving in with good bounce, Duminy closes the face with the intention of working it through mid-wicket but it catches the inside edge and runs down to fine leg for one.
Melinda Farrell, Australian journalist, tweets, "Starc's first over: 147.3, 145.9, 141.5, 147.6, 146.4, 145.9. Good thing he's underdone going into this Test..."
On a length and around off, Elgar gets across a bit and nudges it to fine leg for one.
Inside edge, uppish but it's safe. Back of a length ball darted into the left-hander, Duminy stays back to defend but it comes off the inside half of the bat and speeds past short leg for three runs.
Outside off on a good length, Elgar has an easy leave.
Firdose Moonda, South African journalist, pens in her thoughts with this tweet, "We knew it would come at one stage of the tour but perhaps not this early... suddenly South Africa wish AB was here."

FOUR! Top shot! Once again just the mere push and it has gone for a boundary. Hazlewood drops it full and outside off, Dean with a good positive stride in drives it through the line past the right side of the bowler for a boundary.
Full in length and on off, Elgar gets forward and defends it back to the bowler.
Off the mark! Too straight in line, Josh, around middle on a fuller length and Duminy tickles it through mid-wicket for three runs.
On a length and around middle and off, Duminy fails to defend it off his back foot and is hit on the thigh pad.
Interesting. JP DUMINY walks in at number 4, replacing Amla.

OUT! Amla is a goner! A massive setback for South Africa! Hazlewood may not be as ferocious as Starc with his pace but he is McGrath-esque with his line and length. Hurls it in the good area just outside off, Amla with a tentative footwork has a gentle push inside the line and edges it behind to second slip. Steven Smith is patrolling that region and rest is history. He doesn't drop many. Amla bags a duck and Australia are off to a flier! Damien Fleming on twitter has termed this line from Hazlewood as - Hazlewood hallway of hesitation! Top stuff.

Take that for a reply from the fast bowler. Arrows in a full ball around off, 148.6 kph and curving away a shade off the seam, Elgar tries defending from the crease but is beaten all ends up. This is scintillating battle between bat and ball.

FOUR! Just the touch of the bat and it has raced away to the fence beating the chase given by David Warner, one of the best athletes around. Shows that this outfield is lightning quick as well. Lands it full and outside off, Elgar gets forward and pushes it with excellent timing through covers for a boundary.
Great carry to the keeper. Zippy delivery, on a length and outside off, shaping away, Elgar leaves it alone and Nevill leaps after moving across to his left to collect the ball over his head.
Sharp delivery again, he is bowling fire, keeps his pace in the high 140s, on a length and outside off, Elgar defends it from the crease with a loose bottom hand.
On a good length and around off, Dean defends it off his back foot.

Beautifully bowled by Starc, angles in a full ball on middle and off, nipping away a bit, Elgar is unsure of his footwork, he is neither forward, nor back entirely and gets squared up in defense. It comes off the outside half of the bat and rolls to gully.
Renowned writer, KEVIN MCCALLUM tweets, "It may sound a bit harsh, but Co could have left that Starc delivery on length. Came into his body quickly, though."
Too wide outside off, Amla has an easy leave. Not a very impressive first over by Josh.
On a length and outside off, a little bit of away movement, Amla shoulders arms.
Fullish ball on off, Elgar pushes it softly through extra cover to get off the mark. South Africa are away as well!
Fullish and on middle and off, Elgar stays inside the crease and pushes it out with an angled bat.
This one is closer to the off stump line, Elgar has to play at it and defends it down safely.
A gentle loosener first up, full and wide outside off, Elgar has an easy leave.
Josh Hazlewood to share the new ball from the other end.
Once again it's too wide outside off to make the new batsman play. What a first over!
Wide outside off, on a length, Amla has nothing to do with it.
Hashim Amla walks in next at number 3.

OUT! Mitchel Marsh has taken a stunner! Wow, what a cracking start to the summer for the Aussies. Cook has been cooked very early. Starc delivers a snorter around off, on back of a length again and there is extra bounce too at 147.5 kph. Cook is squared up in defense and the outside edge flies to gully. Mitchell Marsh stationed there dives to his left and takes a stunning two-handed catch. The Aussies are all pumped up and Stephen walks back with a forlorn face.
Terrific delivery, a peach, landing around off on a back of a length and nips away a shade. Cook feels for it, flat-footed and gets beaten.

And now a delivery to remind us of Mitchell Johnson. No not the one to rattle the batsman but the one which can register itself in the useless category. Very wide outside off, lively pace again, 145.9 kph, Cook allows it through with ease.
Excellent pace first up, on a good length and angling away from the batsman, 147.3 kph, Cook covers the line and shoulders arms.

It's play time at the WACA! We are done and dusted with the national anthems. Stephen Cook and Dean Elgar are the South African openers. Mitchell Starc to steam in with the new red cherry. Three slips and a gully in place. Here we go...
Australia - David Warner, Shaun Marsh, Usman Khawaja, Steven Smith(c), Adam Voges, Mitchell Marsh, Peter Nevill(w), Mitchell Starc, Peter Siddle, Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood.
South Africa - Dean Elgar, Stephen Cook, Hashim Amla, Faf du Plessis(c), Jean-Paul Duminy, Temba Bavuma, Quinton de Kock(w), Vernon Philander, Dale Steyn, Kagiso Rabada, Keshav Maharaj.

TOSS - Up goes the coin, Faf du Plessis calls it correctly and SOUTH AFRICA ELECT TO BAT! An expected playing XI for them and the only new face is Keshav Maharaj, who makes his Test debut. Australia announced their XI yesterday itself and have stuck to it.
Weather - Bright and sunny conditions with not a single cloud in the sky. It's a perfect setting and as expected a good crowd has come to watch the first day of the Australian summer.

Plenty of banter heading into this Test series, enough of talks and it's time to walk the talk now. A highly anticipated series is minutes away from getting underway as Australia kickstart their summer. The venue is Perth and a livelier surface is expected to host this electric contest. Hello and a warm welcome everyone for day 1 of the first Test match and thank you for joining us. Stay with us for toss and other updates...
